question: Tell me about a time you raised a new idea and made sure it was heard for at least a few minutes before moving on. What happened?

raiseTranscript.text: In my first project, I noticed our error logging was inconsistent and suggested switching to structured logs during standup. The team wanted to move on but I asked for two minutes to show a quick example of how it would cut debugging time. We discussed it briefly and the lead said we'd try it on the next ticket.
What was the outcome and how did you follow up?
It got adopted after one ticket showed faster root causes. I logged the change in our wiki so others could see it.

Quote: 'I asked for two minutes to show a quick example'

junior.raiseFeedback: Raises the bar on Have Backbone; Disagree and Commit for the question. The candidate described raising structured logging in standup and explicitly asking for two minutes when the team wanted to move on. This shows early ownership of surfacing an improvement and ensuring brief airtime. The follow-up confirmed they tracked the small adoption without claiming broad impact. Biggest strength is the concrete ask for time rather than dropping the idea.

raiseTranscript.text: Our two teams were duplicating API calls for user profiles. I proposed a shared service in a joint planning meeting. When the other lead pushed back on timeline I asked for five minutes to walk through the duplication metrics and a minimal integration path. We agreed to a pilot on one endpoint.
How did you handle the disagreement after the pilot?
After the pilot cut latency 15 percent we committed to the shared approach even though my team had to take on extra initial work.

raiseTranscript.text: We were debating whether to sunset a legacy product line or invest in a new platform. I raised the option of a phased migration in the quarterly offsite. When the room wanted to decide quickly I asked for ten minutes to present retention data and cannibalization risk. The group agreed to a six-month pilot on one segment.
What trade-offs did you commit to after the pilot?
We committed to sunsetting the legacy line on schedule even though it meant short-term revenue pressure in two regions, because the data showed long-term platform health.
